extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, Tribes, and federal agency staff participating in notice-and-comment rulemaking and administrative proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Federal notice-and-comment procedural requirements and expectations for submitting, considering, and responding to public comments across agency rulemakings, environmental reviews, tribal processes, and administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60-day public comment period after Federal Register notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide notice of the opportunity for the public, within 60 days following publication of the Federal Register notice, to submit comment and evidence on whether the request meets [requirements].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in contexts such as Part 50 (procedures for reestablishing government-to-government relationship with the Native Hawaiian community). The 60-day window is the explicit timeframe for public submission of comments and evidence after notice publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary/agency will review and consider public comments in decisionmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary will review and consider public comments in deciding to approve or disapprove [an application/request].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must take submitted comments into account when making approval/disapproval decisions; consideration may include revising proposed actions or documents based on comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide copies of public comments to designated tribal official and consider in final TERA
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will provide copies of the comments to the Designated Tribal Official; the final proposed TERA [Tribal Energy Resource Agreement] may be based on the comments received; if the Tribe revises the TERA based on comments, appropriate follow-up occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to tribal specific procedures (e.g., Part 224). Agencies must share comments with tribal officials and may use comments as the basis for revising proposed agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide notice and at least 30-day comment period for proposed directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Service shall provide notice to the public of a proposed directive or interim directive and provide an opportunity to submit comments during a comment period of not less than 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires agencies to review, consider, and respond to timely comments received. Used in contexts like Forest Service directives and other agency internal directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester has 60 days to respond to timely comments/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester will have 60 days to respond to any comment or evidence that was timely submitted to [the agency].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the requester (e.g., applicant) a fixed period to reply to submitted public comments or evidence before the agency finalizes its decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must solicit comments from federal, state, local agencies, applicants, and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain the comments of any Federal agency which has jurisdiction... Request the comments of: (i) Appropriate State and local agencies... Request comments from the applicant, if any. Request comments from the public, affirmatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA/Environmental Impact Statement contexts: agencies must actively solicit input from relevant governmental entities, applicants, and the public (not merely wait for voluntary submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response obligation in final EIS (consider substantive timely comments and explain disposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider substantive comments timely submitted during the public comment period. The agency shall respond to individual comments or groups of comments in the final environmental [document], including explanations (e.g., corrections or why comments do not warrant further agency response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to final Environmental Impact Statements and similar environmental documents (e.g., CEQ regulations). Response can be to individuals or grouped comments; must explain disposition and whether corrections or further action are warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum 30‑day comment period for significant revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The opportunity to submit written comments on proposed significant revisions shall... A minimum of 30 days [is provided].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to procedures such as Federal Acquisition Regulation/system significant revisions; agencies must provide at least 30 days for public comment on significant changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum 45‑day comment period for certain written comments (petitions, proposed prohibition rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments shall be made ... at least 45 days for submission of written comments concerning a petition for an exemption or concerning a proposed prohibition rule or a Tentative Staff Analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from Department of Energy administrative procedures: certain high‑impact actions require longer comment windows (45 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearings and notice timing (PHA plans): require hearings and pre-hearing notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The governing body must conduct a public hearing to discuss the PHA plan and invite public comment on the plan(s). Not later than 45 days before the public hearing is to take place, the PHA must [provide notice].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to Public Housing Agency plans (HUD): agencies must hold hearings and provide advance public notice (45-day pre-hearing timeline mentioned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and channels for submitting comments (written, email, addressed to offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: E-mail and written comments on voluntary standards from the public to the CPSC shall be [accepted]. Address correspondence to specified offices (e.g., 'Attn: Comment Procedures' or Board of Directors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations often specify acceptable submission methods (email, mail) and where to send comments; follow the agency's stated addressing and filing instructions to ensure comments are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late‑filed comments may be considered if they will assist disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Late-filed comments. [Agency] may consider late-filed comments if [the agency] determines that the comment will assist in the disposition of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While timeliness is required, agencies retain discretion to accept late submissions when they materially aid decisionmaking; however, no entitlement to have late comments considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should encourage maximum practicable public participation and determine when inviting comment is warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures analogous to public rulemaking are intended to encourage the maximum practicable public participation in the Department's rulemaking; determinations as to whether inviting public comment is warranted shall be conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to Department of the Navy examples: agencies should aim to maximize participation but retain internal judgment about when formal comment solicitation is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to comment on draft Environmental Impact Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the Commission to comment on draft environmental impact statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain agencies have explicit policy obligations to provide agency commentary on draft EISs (e.g., NRC policy), reinforcing inter-agency participation in environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for public inspection of applications and ability to file supporting or opposing comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Application available at its offices for public inspection during normal business hours ... Any interested party may file comments with the Agency supporting or opposing an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and gives interested parties the chance to review application materials before submitting comments; typical in grant, program, or facility application processes.
